newsitem.title: USA: Dow seesaws lower, snapping three-session rally.
newsitem.headline: Dow seesaws lower, snapping three-session rally.

text.p: U.S. blue chips ended lower on Monday, pausing in their advance towards yet another market milestone.

The Dow industrials fell 37 points to close unofficially at 7858, as investors cashed in on a blistering three-session run that had placed the blue chip average in striking distance of the 8000 level.
Early in the session, it appeared the mark would topple today, with the Dow racing as high as 7951 in the opening hour. But just as quickly, the rally ran out of steam.
"The market's entitled to a little rest," said Al Goldman, market analyst at A.G. Edwards and Sons. "We've had a one-way trip up."

Analysts attributed much of the market's weakness to routine profit-taking, noting many declining issues were among those that had paced a run that saw the Dow add some 223 points in the last three sessions of last week.
Drug stocks were one such group, with Dow component Merck & Co Inc off 1-11/16 to 103-1/2 and Pfizer Inc down 1-3/4 to 62.
Few analysts thought the market's decline today represented anything more than a brief interruption in the sizzling run that has left most, if not all, of Wall Street's forecasts far behind.
"The bulls are definitely still in charge here," said Greg Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities Inc. "Any profit-taking here is likely to be reasonably contained and very short-term."
But one area of particular weakness for the market came from gold mining shares, which tumbled along with the price of the precious metal today.
Barrick Gold Corp fell 1-11/16 to 20-1/4 and Placer Dome Inc fell 2-3/16 to 14 as gold prices collapsed under the weight of selling by central banks, most recently Australia's.
The August gold contract closed $6.20 lower at $319.00 an ounce, a level not seen since 1985 on New York's Commodity Exchange.

"There's no reason in the world to buy gold at this point," said Goldman. "We don't even have benign inflation, we have declining inflation and there are no world crises to drive people to be buyers."
Barrick and Placer Dome were the NYSE's two most active issues.

American Express Co fell 3-15/16 to 78-5/16, the steepest loss among Dow components, reversing most of a nearly seven-point jump last Thursday sparked by rumors of renewed merger talks between the company and Citicorp.
Citicorp also fell, shedding 1-5/16 to 128-7/16 despite a rally in U.S. Treasuries that drove the yield on the long bond down to 6.58 percent.

Jones Medical Industries Inc tumbled 15-1/2 to 27-7/8 after the company warned of lower than forecast second quarter results. Jones Medical said it still expected to match estimates during the third and fourth quarters.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 3.13 points to 1470.74.
The S&P 500 index fell 4.72 points to 912.20.
